key: helter skelter (1990)(audiogenic)[cr skr][t +3 skr]/Helter Skelter (1990)(Audiogenic)[cr SKR][t +3 SKR].adf:hs:0:0286
name: build_bitplane_copper_list
description: Fills four copper-list entries that each load the high and low words of a bitplane pointer register pair, advancing the pointer by 40 bytes per entry. It then writes the copper end-of-list marker and saves the list start and final pointer in globals.

name: enter_supervisor_and_launch
description: Opens a library by name through the exec base and switches to supervisor state, then sets the enable bit on two stored control words for interrupts and DMA. It copies a block of its own code to low memory and jumps through an entry obtained from the opened library.

name: describe_undecompiled_routine
description: The decompiler timed out, so no body is available for this 18-instruction routine. It is reached only through a pc-relative address and called from one other routine, which is all the evidence shows.

name: reset_chipset_and_clear_memory
description: Copies two saved words into a state block, writes all-clear masks to the interrupt and DMA control words, and clears 2000 longwords at a fixed address. It then calls one routine and re-enables DMA with the set bit and the standard enable bits.

name: read_serial_byte_and_handshake
description: Clears a pending interrupt request flag, then if the serial input register holds a byte it reads it, pulses the serial control register to acknowledge it, and returns the byte. For three specific byte values it also toggles a bit in one of two stored words, and it returns zero when no byte is waiting.

name: poll_until_result_zero
description: Calls one unnamed routine in a loop until it returns zero, then returns. The only evidence is that loop and the single callee.

name: copy_strided_longword_column
description: Copies seven longwords from a source block at 60-byte intervals into a destination at 40-byte intervals, with the starting offsets passed in registers. It returns once the seven copies are done.

name: poll_nested_until_zero
description: Calls one unnamed routine repeatedly until its second result register is zero, and repeats that inner loop until the first result is zero. It returns after both conditions hold.

name: copy_strided_byte_column
description: Copies seven bytes from a source block at 60-byte intervals into a destination at 40-byte intervals, with both offsets passed in registers. It returns after the seven stores.

name: read_loader_and_relocate
description: Fills in an I/O request's length, data address and offset fields with a read command, then sends it through the library's do-I/O entry. It then writes stored values to the interrupt and DMA control registers, sets the drive control register, copies loader code to low memory and jumps to it.

name: copy_loader_and_jump
description: Writes stored values to the interrupt and DMA control registers and sets the drive control register. If a stored flag is zero, it copies a block of loader code to low memory and jumps into it.

description: Updates a table byte and a control word, then checks a value against a two-word bounds pair and raises the check trap if it is outside. Otherwise it toggles one bit in a byte, selected by a register, and clears bits in a longword before stopping at bad instruction data.

description: Copies a byte and a longword from a source pointer to two offsets of a second pointer, then ORs a register value into a byte of the source. The decoding stops at bad instruction data, so the routine is incomplete.

name: compute_flags_and_store_byte
description: Builds a flag value from a register byte and stores it as a masked word in a block addressed from another register. It then stores a byte from a table into a computed address and stops at bad instruction data, so the routine is incomplete.

description: The listed facts give only two instructions and one call to a tiny OR routine, which does not match the long pseudo-code. That pseudo-code shows a bit-driven loop copying bytes backward through a packed stream, so the decode is unreliable and only the copy structure is described.

description: The pseudo-code shows a bit-driven loop that refills a bit buffer from the packed stream and copies runs of bytes backward into a destination. Its facts list 159 instructions and one unnamed caller.

name: read_previous_longword_shifted
description: Reads the longword just before an address register's position, shifts it right by one bit, sets its top bit, and returns the result. One unnamed routine calls it.

key: conqueror (1989)(rainbow arts)(de-en)[cr qtx][h tfs]/Conqueror (1989)(Rainbow Arts)(De-En)[cr QTX][h TFS].adf:game:0:00CE
name: advance_bit_buffer_by_count
description: Shifts a bit buffer right by a count taken from a register, refilling it from the previous longword with its top bit set whenever it empties. It returns no value.

name: poll_button_then_setup
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then checks a status bit repeatedly and returns once it reads clear. The listed facts show access to the first CIA port register and the vertical position register, plus six unnamed callees.

name: clear_memory_and_build_copper
description: Clears a flag, zeroes 2048 longwords at a fixed address, and copies a template into a list that it fills with generated wait and move entries. It finishes by storing the list addresses in globals, and its facts show the copper and DMA and interrupt control registers in use.

name: fill_copper_list_from_table
description: Returns early unless a flag is zero, then walks a table of 144 entries, computing a word from each entry's low bits and a running offset. For each entry it writes three words derived from that value at fixed offsets in a list, advancing the table pointer and wrapping to a fixed address at the end.

name: advance_sequence_and_copy_entries
description: Advances a sequence index held in a global, wrapping at a sentinel value, then copies values from the sequence into a list at a stride of twelve words. The copy count is taken from the index.

name: program_blitter_from_table
description: Waits until the blitter is idle, then sets its source, destination, modulo, mask, control and size registers. It searches a table for a matching byte and uses the match index to choose the blit destination before starting the blit.

name: set_blit_destination_fixed
description: The listed facts mark this two-instruction block as reached only because a gap decodes as code. Its body computes a destination from a 128-byte stride, writes several fixed blitter-style words, and wraps a pointer when a stored byte is zero, and it calls one unnamed routine.

name: copy_table_pairs_into_buffers
description: Copies sixteen table values into two buffers, one walking backward and one forward at a stride of eight bytes. Afterwards it decrements a counter and, when the counter reaches zero, resets it and advances the table pointer by one entry, wrapping at a sentinel value, with modulo, display-control, copper and interrupt registers listed in the facts.

name: describe_undecompiled_routine
description: The pseudo-code is unavailable for this single-instruction routine, because decompilation timed out. Its facts show only an absolute-move address reference and two unnamed callers.

name: copy_bytes_and_reset_pointers
description: Copies one byte at a time from a source region into a fixed low-memory buffer until the source pointer reaches a fixed end address. It then stores the buffer address in two globals, calls one unnamed routine, and returns zero.

name: copy_longwords_then_call
description: If the destination pointer passed on the stack is non-null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset of a base register into it. It then calls a routine held in an address register, which the facts name as find_max_and_prepare_buffer.

key: anarchy (1991)(psygnosis)[cr defjam - ccs][t +7 defjam - ccs]/Anarchy (1991)(Psygnosis)[cr Defjam - CCS][t +7 Defjam - CCS].adf:Anarchy:0:0000
name: unpack_compressed_program_entry
description: Program entry that first copies a block of data into memory, then unpacks a bit-packed stream backward using literal bytes and back-references. A later loop walks the unpacked output and handles a marker byte, and the facts show COLOR00 touched and four unnamed callees.

key: anarchy (1991)(psygnosis)[cr defjam - ccs][t +7 defjam - ccs]/Anarchy (1991)(Psygnosis)[cr Defjam - CCS][t +7 Defjam - CCS].adf:Anarchy:0:0070
name: read_store_previous_longword
description: Reads the longword just before an address register's position, stores its low byte through a pointer, and returns it shifted right by one bit with the top bit set. Four unnamed routines reference it, and it calls three unnamed routines.

key: anarchy (1991)(psygnosis)[cr defjam - ccs][t +7 defjam - ccs]/Anarchy (1991)(Psygnosis)[cr Defjam - CCS][t +7 Defjam - CCS].adf:Anarchy:0:0096
name: advance_bit_buffer_by_count
description: Shifts a bit buffer right by a count taken from a register, calling an unnamed refill routine each time the buffer empties. It returns no value.

name: init_display_and_load_palette
description: Calls the exec forbid routine, clears a block of longwords, and copies a table to low memory. It then writes sixteen color register values from a fixed table, sets sprite and second-copper pointers and display control registers, and has ten unnamed callees.

name: write_register_words_to_global
description: Writes eight 16-bit values taken from two input registers to one global location, in the order the code gives. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: pause_with_delay_loops
description: Runs six passes, each calling one unnamed routine and then a long countdown loop, which together make a timed pause. The facts show one caller and one unnamed callee.

name: pause_with_delay_loops
description: Runs six passes, each calling one unnamed routine and then a long countdown loop, which together make a timed pause. The facts show one caller and one unnamed callee.

name: build_plane_copper_entries
description: Writes a copper header with a display control word derived from a count register, then writes one bitplane pointer move pair per plane. Each plane's pointer advances by a stride held in a register.

name: build_sprite_copper_entries
description: Writes eight sprite pointer move pairs into a copper list, one per sprite, taking each 32-bit pointer from a source table. The entries step through the sprite pointer registers in order.

name: set_display_window_registers
description: Writes four display window and data fetch start and stop values, then clears four bitplane control and modulo words, all through one base register. The routine has one caller.

name: save_interrupt_state_and_enable
description: Stores the current interrupt-enable value in two saved slots, installs a routine as the handler, and writes a fixed enable mask to the interrupt control register. It calls one unnamed routine.

name: disable_master_interrupts
description: Writes a fixed value to the interrupt enable register with the set bit clear, which disables the master interrupt switch. It has one caller.

name: decrement_counter_then_clear_requests
description: Decrements a counter if it is nonzero, calls two unnamed routines, then writes a fixed value that clears three audio request bits in the interrupt request register. The routine's address is taken by an absolute move, and one routine calls it.

name: clear_global_and_call_repeatedly
description: Writes zero to a global and then calls one unnamed routine four times in sequence. It has one caller.

name: fill_seven_byte_records
description: Fills a fixed number of seven-byte records, each holding bytes derived from a running value and an unnamed routine's result, a zero byte, and a longword taken from a register. The running value increases by one after each record.

name: mix_seed_from_raster_position
description: Updates a seed longword by XOR and addition with a table value and a constant, mixing in a value read from the vertical position register. It then advances the table pointer by two bytes.

name: add_strided_table_offsets
description: Adds 4, 3, 2 and 1 in turn to bytes at intervals of eight bytes across four separate tables, each with a fixed entry count. It has one caller.

name: read_keyboard_serial_with_delay
description: When a delay counter is zero, reads the keyboard serial byte, inverts it, shifts it into a stored value, and reloads the counter with a long delay when the low bit is clear. When the counter is nonzero it only decrements it, and the facts list the keyboard serial register as touched.

name: dispatch_pending_key_code
description: Acts on a pending key value using a per-entry type table: one type writes several words and another toggles a flag while calling three unnamed routines. The two special codes adjust a stored index within bounds and then call the same routines.

name: set_three_constant_globals
description: Writes three constant values to globals, and the pseudo-code shows nothing more. The facts list 89 instructions and three unnamed callees, so the pseudo-code is probably incomplete.

name: emit_string_with_escapes
description: Walks a zero-terminated byte string, calling an unnamed routine for each character. A marker byte of minus two instead looks up a code in a table and calls the routine 44 times for that entry.

name: copy_table_row_by_character
description: Maps a zero character to a letter O, searches a fixed character list for the input, then copies seven bytes spaced 44 bytes apart from the table entry at the matching index into a destination. It has two callers.

name: copy_seven_strided_bytes
description: Copies seven bytes from a source at intervals of 44 bytes to a destination at the same intervals. It has one caller.

key: midwinter (1990)(microprose)(en)[cr defjam - ccs - acc][h timecircle]/Midwinter (1990)(MicroProse)(En)[cr Defjam - CCS - ACC][h Timecircle].adf:bootblock:0:000C
name: load_boot_disk_blocks
description: Boot-block entry that copies a small routine into low memory, opens a library by name, and issues three disk read requests with fixed lengths and offsets. It then inverts a block of bytes it just loaded, closes the library, and issues a final request whose result decides whether it returns, with DMA writes listed in the facts.

name: apply_palette_when_flagged
description: Checks a flag bit, and when it is set advances a state value and calls a routine. When the state is zero it copies sixteen values, each doubled, into the colour registers and clears four words, then clears the flag; the facts also list the interrupt request register and eight unnamed callees.

name: fill_counting_bytes_or_lookup
description: When a magic value matches, either fills 32 bytes with counting values followed by a sentinel byte, or looks up three table bytes for an index and stores them with fixed values.

name: step_shift_register_lookup
description: When the value is nonzero, rotates its low byte right by one bit, exclusive-ORs a constant, and uses the result as an index into a byte table to store an entry, with a flagged variant for the upper half of the index range. A zero value is cleared.

name: compute_two_position_words
description: Computes two words from an input value and writes them through a pointer, the second word using a carry from the first. A value of two skips the writes, and the input is cleared on return, with the joystick test register listed in the facts.

name: clamp_value_into_range
description: When the value equals one, halves it and subtracts a fixed offset, then clamps it into a fixed range with a second range check. If neither clamp applied it stores minus one, otherwise it clears the value.

name: set_global_minus_one
description: Writes a minus-one value to one global location and returns. The facts mark this as code that a gap decodes, so its caller is not shown.

name: accumulate_signed_input_deltas
description: Sets bits in a flag byte when a status byte is nonzero, then adds the input value, negated when the status byte is set, to two accumulator words, and clears the status byte. The code does not show what the accumulators are used for.

name: decode_joystick_movement_bits
description: Decodes two direction bits from an input word read from the joystick port movement register, and sets a flag bit when the fire-button bit reads clear. It adds signed movement from the decoded bits to two accumulators, with the fire-button port register also listed in the facts.

name: decode_mouse_movement_bits
description: Decodes mouse movement from an input word read from the mouse port movement register, setting flag bits when the button bits read clear. It adds signed high-byte deltas to two accumulators, and the facts also list the button register.

name: dispatch_by_two_bit_state
description: Reads the two low bits of a byte as a state and maps set bits to a minus-one value, then, if two longword fields of the input record are not both zero, calls through a table entry indexed by that state. The decompiler could not resolve the table target.

name: enable_audio_dma_or_clear
description: When a stored state is zero, sets it to a DMA control value, calls through it, makes four unnamed calls and then calls it again. Otherwise it clears four state words; the facts list the four audio volume registers and the DMA control register.

name: set_audio_period_constants
description: Writes a few constant values to globals, including a pointer to one of them. The facts show the period registers of two audio channels and the DMA control register, and mark this as code that a gap decodes.

name: stub_empty_return
description: A single return instruction with no other behaviour, executed in the reference run.

name: find_highest_set_bit_lookup
description: If a flag byte is nonzero, clears the flag, scans the bits of an input byte from the top for the first set one, and loads a longword from a table indexed by that bit number. If no bit is set the index is left at its last value.

name: load_audio_channel_record
description: Sets two constant globals, then reads a fixed-size record selected by a three-bit index and stores its fields in globals, including two longwords and three words. The facts show the channel zero period register and the DMA control register, and mark this as code that a gap decodes.

name: test_bit_then_reset_state
description: Tests one bit of an inverted input byte and, when it is set, stores a group of constant values and a routine reference. It then clears a mask derived from the byte and stores zero; the facts show the channel zero volume register, the text fragment NuNu/, and one unnamed callee.

name: set_indexed_bit_then_call

description: Writes a value with bit seven clear to a control byte, then clears bit three of it. It has one caller.

name: set_bit_two_by_parity
description: Sets bit two of a byte when a counter is even and clears it when the counter is odd, writing through a base address. It has one caller.

name: pause_with_countdown
description: Counts a word variable down from 3072 to minus one as a timed pause, then returns. Two unnamed routines call it.
